title: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan announce Mecca agreement
gist: A 3:39 Al-Monitor 'Middle East Minute' podcast page whose only substantive text is the episode blurb: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan have announced a Mecca agreement, and the kingdom is reportedly expecting attacks from Iraqi militias and the Houthis as the Yemen conflict heats up. The page is otherwise player boilerplate, so there is no argument or evidence beyond those two facts.

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan have announced an agreement concluded in Mecca, grouping the Gulf's leading oil exporter with the region's largest non-Arab military power and a nuclear-armed South Asian state.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A Riyadh-Ankara-Islamabad bloc would reshape Gulf security procurement and hedging away from sole US dependence; watch for defense and manpower clauses as they surface.
insights.quote: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan announce Mecca agreement

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia is reportedly expecting attacks from Iraqi militias and the Houthis, indicating the kingdom anticipates a two-front proxy threat on its northern and southern flanks simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Direct strikes on Saudi territory are the tail risk that reprices crude and Gulf credit; anticipated attacks argue for elevated insurance and air-defense spending regardless of whether they land.
insights.quote: The kingdom is reportedly expecting attacks from Iraqi militias and the Houthis
insights.locator: The kingdom is reportedly expecting attacks

insights.claim: The conflict in Yemen is heating up at the same time as the announced Mecca agreement, tying the new alignment's first test to an active war on Saudi Arabia's southern border.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Yemen escalation is the near-term trigger to monitor for Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab shipping disruption layered on top of Gulf risk.
insights.quote: while the conflict in Yemen heats up
insights.locator: The kingdom is reportedly expecting attacks
